files_downloaded.note: downloaded for comparison; superseded by the *_modifiedreplacedmissingrows.txt version below, which NOAA published later (2017-06-27) restoring 64 rows missing from this original 2015 file. Not used in the final analysis.
NOAA-corrected 2015 file (1963 rows vs 1899 in the original goes-xrs-report_2015.txt) -- used in place of the original for data completeness

partial year, 2017-01-04 through 2017-06-28 -- this is the LAST file NOAA ever published in the legacy goes-xrs-report_*.txt format before it was retired at the GOES-15(legacy)->GOES-16/17(GOES-R/EXIS) transition; no full-year 2017 or any 2018+ file exists in this format on the NGDC archive (confirmed by directory listing: last annual file is goes-xrs-report_2017-ytd.txt / goes-xrs-report_2017-input-ytd.txt, both dated 2017-07-06).

file_format.description: Fixed-width text, 110 characters/line, one flare event per line. Verified by direct byte-offset inspection of raw file content (not assumed from secondary documentation).

columns_used.[0:11]: station/date code, e.g. '31777140101'; substring [5:11] = YYMMDD event date
columns_used.[13:17]: event BEGIN time, HHMM UT -- this is the timestamp used as the event time for the SOC pipeline
columns_used.[18:22]: event END time, HHMM UT (not used)
columns_used.[23:27]: event MAX (peak) time, HHMM UT (not used)
columns_used.[28:34]: heliographic location, blank if undetermined (not used)
columns_used.[59:65]: GOES flare class letter + 2-digit mantissa, e.g. 'C 32' = C3.2 (recorded for provenance/context only, not used by the pipeline)
columns_used.[67:70]: reporting GOES satellite code, e.g. 'G15' -- used as the single-instrument filter

file_format.validation: 0 malformed date/time fields out of 5925 raw lines scanned across all 4 downloaded files (regex-validated 6-digit date, 4-digit time, hour<=23, minute<=59); all lines exactly 110 chars; station code field [0:5] constant '31777' across every line in every file.

instrument_continuity_check.finding: The raw combined 2014-2017(ytd) catalog is NOT single-satellite: alongside GOES-15 (G15), a small fraction of events are individually reported against GOES-13 (G13) or GOES-14 (G14) -- these were operating in parallel as backup/secondary XRS platforms throughout this era (NOT a primary-satellite handover; GOES-15 remained NOAA SWPC's PRIMARY XRS satellite continuously from 2010 through the 2018 GOES-16 handover). Raw per-year satellite counts: {"G15": 5782, "G13": 76, "G14": 67}.
instrument_continuity_check.decision: Filtered the entire 2014-2017(ytd) dataset to GOES-15 (G15) -reported events ONLY, dropping the small G13/G14 backup-reported fraction (76+67=143 of 5925 raw events, 2.4%), to guarantee every event analyzed comes from the SAME physical XRS instrument/satellite for the entire PRE+POST window -- this is a strictly stronger continuity guarantee than just avoiding the GOES-15(legacy)->GOES-16/17(GOES-R) design change that METHODOLOGY_NOTE.md flags as the primary confounder risk.

maximum.precision: month-level only -- NASA/NOAA solar cycle panels report cycle maxima/minima as the month in which the 13-month-smoothed sunspot number peaks/troughs; no finer (day-level) official date exists for this quantity
sources: https://www.sidc.be/SILSO/news004 (SIDC: '2014: maximum year for solar cycle 24')

minimum.note: NOT used as a segment boundary here -- this is exactly the minimum that crosses the GOES-15(legacy)->GOES-16/17(GOES-R/EXIS) satellite/instrument transition that METHODOLOGY_NOTE.md flags as a confounder risk, and the legacy goes-xrs-report_*.txt format itself stops being published mid-2017, well before Dec 2019. Reported here only for context.

segment_definition.convention_used: PRE = ASCENDING-phase events immediately preceding the documented cycle-24 maximum (all available GOES-15 events in the downloaded window before 2014-04-01T00:00:00Z); POST = DECLINING-phase events following the maximum through the end of available single-instrument (GOES-15, legacy report format) data. This is the 'ascending period leading to the max' alternative explicitly permitted by METHODOLOGY_NOTE.md gap (d), chosen because the task's downloaded window (2014-2017 only, per instructions) leaves only ~3 months of GOES-15 data before 2014-04-01 -- there being no 2010-2013 files in this run's downloaded set, PRE is necessarily short and entirely the January-March 2014 ascending-phase tail leading into the panel-dated maximum.

post_primary.rule: all G15 events with begin-time >= 2014-04-01T00:00:00Z, through end of available single-instrument legacy-format data

pre_robustness.rule: most-recent 50% by event COUNT of pre_primary (closest to the transition)

post_robustness.rule: 50% by event COUNT of post_primary nearest the transition

mundane_mechanism_check.a_priori_flag: detection bias toward small flares dependent on X-ray background flux (higher at solar max, i.e. in PRE here); not corrected in this run, reported as observed.
mundane_mechanism_check.observation: mu (mean event rate, events/day) real_pre=6.97, real_post=4.35 (primary); event counts drop from 625 (PRE, 3 months) at cycle max to a much larger absolute POST count (5157, ~3.25 years, PRE ascending tail near max still fairly active) but LOWER per-day rate in POST as expected declining toward the 2017 near-minimum -- consistent with the a-priori-flagged direction (more/higher-background flares reported near max) and not obviously structurally anomalous.
